'''''Brachychiton discolor''''' is a rainforest tree of eastern [[Australia]]. It grows in drier rainforest areas. Scattered from [[Paterson, New South Wales]] (32° S) to [[Mackay, Queensland]] (21° S), there is also an isolated community of these trees on [[Cape York Peninsula]] in tropical Queensland.

Common names include '''lacebark tree''', '''lace kurrajong''', '''pink kurrajong''', '''scrub bottle tree''', '''white kurrajong''', '''hat tree''' and '''sycamore'''.

== Description ==
''Brachychiton discolor'' is a tree that grows up to {{convert|30|m|-1}} tall. It has pink flowers without petals. The trunk is straight, grey and cylindrical, up to {{convert|75|cm|in|abbr=on|-1}} in diameter. It is not buttressed at the base. The twigs are hairy, brown and smooth.

The leaves are hairy and lobed with three, five or seven points. They are {{convert|10|-|20|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, whitish underneath and dark green above. Leaf veins are visible on both sides.

Flowers form from November to February. They are pink, almost without stalks and {{convert|3|-|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter. Male and female flowers are separate and without petals. The fruit is a hairy boat-shaped [[follicle (fruit)|follicle]] maturing from December to July. It is {{convert|7|-|20|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long, containing up to 30 seeds, each {{convert|9|mm|in|abbr=on}} long. Germination from fresh seed occurs without difficulty.

== Uses ==
''Brachychiton discolor'' is widely planted as an ornamental tree. The wood is used to make shields by [[Indigenous Australians]]. The roasted seeds are edible to humans.
